title: Fix unicode token-gap handling in constraint muxer and stabilize streaming for tool calls
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fix: Constraint muxer tokenization alignment; improved streaming stability for tool/function call frames; no user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: This PR fixes a class of failures where grammar/regex-based constrained decoders produced invalid or truncated structured output for inputs containing multi-codepoint Unicode sequences (emoji, combined marks) due to a token-gap mismatch between the tokenizer and the constraint backends. The change introduces a boundary-aware token mapping layer in the constraint muxer and a conservative fallback to byte-level regex matching when tokenization ambiguities would otherwise break streaming/tool-call framing.

Motivation and context: In production we've seen intermittent failures when customers submit prompts with emoji or complex combining characters. Those inputs sometimes produced malformed structured outputs (missing closing tags, tool-call payload split across streaming frames) because the constraint engine assumed token boundaries that the tokenizer split differently, especially for certain BPE and byte-level encodings. This manifested as downstream JSON parsing errors or tool invocation failures, and was surfaced by ENG-2981 and a recent incident (linked in the Linear ticket).

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds a Unicode-aware boundary resolver that maps character/grapheme cluster boundaries to token index ranges and exposes a confidence score for ambiguous splits. 2) Updates the constraint muxer to use boundary anchors when applying CFG/grammar and regex constraints so that constraints align with grapheme clusters instead of naive byte offsets. 3) Implements a safe fallback: when the boundary confidence is low (e.g., ambiguous tokenizer split on combining marks), the muxer falls back to a byte-level regex mode that preserves streaming framing for tool/function calls and avoids mid-token split tool-call frames. 4) Stabilizes streaming by ensuring streaming frames do not cut tool-call payloads; we now buffer and reframe partial tokens until a safe boundary is reached. 5) Adds regression test coverage and a micro-benchmark demonstrating the perf delta for worst-case Unicode inputs and the improvement in failure-rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for boundary resolver and muxer logic
- [x] Integration tests for streaming tool calls with Unicode prompts
- [x] Micro-benchmark and perf numbers added
- [x] Docs note describing tokenizer-edgecase behaviour and recommended prompt patterns
- [x] QA run in staging (no regressions observed)

Commits (summary):
- 7f3a2b0: introduce boundary_resolver module with grapheme cluster to token mapping and confidence scoring
- 9d12c1f: integrate boundary anchors into constraint_muxer and update CFG/regex application codepaths
- b8a4e2d: implement byte-level regex fallback and streaming reframing for tool calls
- c0f4a5b: tests + fixtures for emoji/combining marks and updated test harness
- d41f6e3: docs + release notes + small lint and CI fixes

Changed areas/files (high level):
- src/constraints/constraint_muxer.py: add boundary-aware matching, fallback mode, and streaming reframing logic
- src/tokenizer/boundary_resolver.cpp and src/tokenizer/boundary_resolver.h: grapheme cluster detection and token index mapping
- src/streaming/stream_framer.rs: buffer/reframe logic to avoid splitting tool-call payloads mid-token
- tests/constraints/test_unicode_boundaries.py: regression tests and fuzz inputs
- tests/streaming/test_tool_call_framing.py: integration tests simulating chunked streaming over sockets
- docs/api/structured_output.md: note on tokenizer edge cases and how muxer handles ambiguous boundaries
- benchmarks/unicode_token_gap/README.md and harness: micro-benchmarks and results

Performance and safety notes:
- The boundary resolver computes grapheme cluster boundaries using ICU algorithms; to avoid a large runtime regression we cache recent mappings per-request and only run the full grapheme scan when a prompt contains multi-codepoint sequences. Benchmarked on p4d.24xlarge: worst-case overhead ~3-7% p99 lat for pathological inputs; average impact <1% for normal traffic.
- The byte-level regex fallback is more conservative and slightly more permissive; it is only used when the confidence heuristic indicates potential split ambiguity.

Tests and QA:
- Added deterministic unit tests covering sequences: emoji with skin-tone modifiers, base + combining marks, ZWJ sequences, and rare Unicode normalization forms.
- Added an integration test that streams a tool call split across many small chunks to validate reframing logic and verify no mid-token tool-call payload is emitted.
- Ran the new tests against mainline models (gpt-family-sim) and verified no difference in outputs for ascii-only prompts.

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Carlos Rivera (review): "Good catch on the grapheme clusters. Two asks: tighten the confidence heuristic threshold and add a short comment explaining why we prefer byte-fallback rather than rewriting tokenizer behavior."
- Maya Chen (author): "Lowered threshold to 0.6 per perf discussion; added explanation in boundary_resolver.h and a short section in docs explaining tradeoffs."
- Sasha Ivanov (review): "Streaming reframer looks sane; can we add a unit test that simulates a partial tool-call payload and ensures the muxer delays emission until safe boundary?"
- Maya Chen: "Added tests/streaming/test_tool_call_framing.py which does exactly that."
- Elena Park (approval): "Tests look comprehensive, benchmarks acceptable, approving."

CI summary:
- Build matrix: linux/macos, python tests, rust streaming runner, C++ boundary module compiled under both clang and gcc
- Initial CI run had a flaky fuzz test failure; rerun passed. All gates green on merge date.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merge commit body: consolidated commits and a short changelog entry.

Related work:
- Follow-on: ENG-3140 will evaluate moving parts of the boundary resolver into a shared tokenizer plugin to avoid repetition across runtimes (tracked as a follow-up).
- This PR was coordinated with SDK teams to ensure no changes required in SDK framing (redwood-sdk-python/TS no-op changes).

Why this is safe for backport:
- No public API changes; behavior is strictly safer (fewer malformed outputs).

Backport candidates: release/1.8.x if customers on that branch reported Unicode failures.

Notes for release notes and customer comms:
- User-visible: better handling of emoji and combined characters in structured outputs and fewer streaming tool-call failures for such prompts. No action required from customers.
